Thursday, November 5, 2026 Sign in / Join Facebook Instagram Linkedin Mail Spotify X Youtube Nigeria Africa World Business and Tech Politics Sports Languages Yoruba Igbo Hausa French Arabic Fulfulde Kiswahili Mandarin connect Home World India Approves $1.53 Billion Energy Storage Scheme World India Approves $1.53 Billion Energy Storage Scheme November 5, 2026 Share Facebook X Pinterest WhatsApp The Indian government has approved a 1.53-billion-dollar scheme to develop 92 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of energy storage capacity.
The move aims to strengthen the country’s energy security and support its renewable energy expansion.
The scheme, approved on Wednesday, will support the development of 60 GWh of hydro pumped storage capacity, 30 GWh of battery energy storage systems and two GWh of alternative energy storage technologies, according to an official government statement.
The initiative is also designed to strengthen India’s domestic energy storage manufacturing industry through financial support for local producers and reduce the country’s dependence on imported components.
Energy storage is considered crucial to managing the intermittent supply of renewable energy, particularly solar and wind power, by storing excess electricity for use when generation is low or demand is high.
The investment comes as India pursues an ambitious target of achieving 500 gigawatts of non-fossil fuel-based electricity capacity by 2030.
The government expects the scheme to encourage private-sector investment, promote technological development and improve the reliability of the country’s power supply as it transitions towards cleaner energy sources.
